What this is, and what it is not

  • Prices are monthly and about 132 days old. They come from SEC Form N-PORT fund holdings, the only free per-CUSIP source. Every price shown is that mark aged onto today's curve — an estimate, never a quote.
  • The credit signal is unvalidated. The backtest can measure relative value (cheap bonds beat rich ones by ~27bp per month, monotonically across quintiles), but the model's implied rating does not predict forward spread change. Treat the credit column as a description, not a forecast.
  • 100% of rows carry a rating cap — mostly because the issuer could not be identified. A capped row still shows its uncapped rating; the cap says the data does not support acting on it.
  • No agency ratings, no true OAS, no covenants. Z-spread stands in for OAS, so callable bonds priced above par are systematically overstated and are capped.

Mean score by category
